A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wikipedia quality-audit and filtering study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, with retained material identifiable despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original Wikipedia filtering and clustering analyses, downstream monolingual and XLM-R experiments, and partition-based experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds random-filter controls, quality and bot-content correlations, and zero-shot and multilingual experiments, with detailed results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The proposed script filtering, exact-match and MinHash deduplication, heuristic classes, and automatic KDE thresholding remain unchanged. V1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix B specify the same threshold procedure. The added multilingual BERT experiments extend evaluation rather than modify the filtering method.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original reported downstream benchmarks and adds Belebele reading comprehension and XNLI natural-language inference. Multilingual Wikipedia pretraining and English-trained zero-shot evaluation substantially broaden coverage: Tables 13–15 report Belebele results for 17 adapted-model and 55 multilingual-model languages, and XNLI results for 15 languages.

E2.justification: V2 adds random filtering as a comparator throughout the retained monolingual comparisons (Tables 8–11), directly testing whether quality-based selection differs from random selection. Section 4.2 additionally compares the filtering-based quality measure with DEPTH+. The existing XLM-R baseline and filtering variants are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a random-article control, English fine-tuning followed by zero-shot testing, and three multilingual BERT models trained for an equal 200,000 steps. V1's equal-character high/low partition design is removed. Existing monolingual and XLM-R/SIB200 settings remain substantially unchanged. The random control's size matching is unclear because its sample size is described as the number of articles 'filtered'.

E4.justification: V1's per-heuristic saliency experiments using high/low partitions disappear, including Section 5.1.2, Figure 6, and Appendix B results. V2 adds random-selection controls and substantial validation analyses relating filtering to DEPTH+ and estimated bot content (Sections 4.2–4.3), including a separate analysis of MinHash's association with bot content.

E5.justification: Five-run reporting and the existing ± values are retained for monolingual results and extended to the random comparator. However, the explicit five-run statement for XLM-R/SIB200 disappears from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 12. V2 reports coefficients and p-values for its new correlations, while new zero-shot tables provide point estimates without run counts or uncertainty.

E6.justification: Shared per-language scores in v1 Tables 2–6 are unchanged in v2 Tables 8–12. V2 adds random-control and zero-shot results: Table 13 reports raw/primary/heuristic averages of 0.25/0.30/0.25, and Table 14 reports 0.44/0.43/0.42. V1's partition results are removed. V2's new Table 2 also contains a reporting inconsistency: its SIB200 random and heuristic averages are 0.63 and 0.50, whereas averaging Table 11's entries gives approximately 0.50 and 0.62, respectively.

T1.justification: The heuristic-score equation and mathematical thresholding procedure are retained. V2's additional equation restates the previously published DEPTH+ metric for an empirical comparison; it introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about Wikipedia quality problems, resource-efficient filtering, and language/task-specific quality remain, including an essentially unchanged abstract. V2 modestly broadens the introduction's stated contribution to recommendations for dataset creation as well as pretraining. The pipeline release becomes an explicit contribution item but was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 revises v1's pessimistic interpretation of filtering Tier 4 Wikipedias and recommends filtering particularly for lower-tier adaptation and zero-shot use. It adds explanations involving article-level versus training-chunk mismatch, multilingual interactions, and heuristic limitations. The discussion also expands to when templatic articles can help dataset annotation and distinguishes collaborative quality from individual-article quality.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix A adds multilingual tokenization and training details, including a 110k WordPiece vocabulary, sampling temperature, training budget, language list, and four H100 GPUs. It also documents Belebele fine-tuning settings and discloses single-GPU monolingual training. Existing monolingual vocabulary estimates and core settings are retained; the repository link identifies the same project.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning through its DEPTH+ comparison and explicit discussion of how its thresholding relates to FineWeb and its pipeline to CulturaX and MADLAD-400. It adds relevant benchmark and training references while removing v1's broader discussion of instruction-tuning evidence and criticisms of data filtering, including the Goldberg and Rogers references.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, heuristic interpretation, experimental narrative, and discussion undergo extensive rewriting. Section 4 gains a new subsection structure, Section 6 becomes Discussion and Recommendations, and the appendices are reorganized around consolidated settings and results. The title also gains a descriptive subtitle.

P2.justification: Detailed main-text result tables move to Appendix A, while v2 introduces a summary table and multiple performance and distribution plots. The pipeline diagram is revised, the saliency boxplot is removed, and the unchanged heuristic distributions move from Figure 4 to Figure 5. V2 Figure 7 introduces a caption inconsistency: its axes show data remaining, while the caption describes data removed.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful validation through DEPTH+/bot comparisons and actual zero-shot and multilingual pretraining tests, strengthening evidence for the paper's intended applications. The net gain is limited by removal of the size-matched saliency study, ambiguous matching of the new random control, and reporting errors: Table 2's SIB200 row conflicts with Table 11, and Figure 7's caption contradicts its axes.
